title: Adequacy
body:
Adequacy is a regulatory-focused module, helping clients meet CMS standards when submitting Medicare Advantage (MA) bids or expansion. It helps health plans evaluate their provider networks against CMS-defined network adequacy standards, including minimum provider counts and access requirements based on time and distance. It highlights provider or access gaps by county and specialty to help prevent failed submissions or missed service area expansions.

Accessing Adequacy

 To navigate to the Adequacy module, on the left-hand sidebar navigation panel, click on Compliance and then select Adequacy from the menu. Adequacy Analyses The Manage Adequacy Analyses page is the default landing page. From here, you can create a new analysis using the Add New Analysis button or create a new Model Network using the Add New Model Network button. This page also displays the list of all previously created Adequacy analyses. Search can be narrowed down by selecting a Specialty Mapping or Network from the dropdown. Creating New Analysis To create a new Adequacy analysis, click on Add New Analysis button. The New Adequacy Analysis criteria page opens. 1. Enter a Name and an optional Description. 2. Select a Base Network and optionally select a Comparison Network . The Base Network is required, and it is the network that is being analyzed to determine if it meets adequacy requirements. Selecting a Comparison Network can help to evaluate how the client’s MA network compares to another competitor’s network. 3. Select the appropriate Adequacy Specification. If there are additional options in the drop-down, see the Adequacy and Accessibility section below. Once a specification is selected, the View icon (eye) adjacent to the Adequacy Specification field is enabled. Clicking on the View icon opens that specifications page which contains the standards of the selected specification . 4. When a CMS Specification is selected, Telehealth specialties can be optionally included in the report. Including Telehealth specialties can boost adequacy score. Requirements given by CMS state that if the network provides telehealth for CMS-defined specialties or provides care (CON = Certificate of Need) in certain counties then they will get an extra 10% bonus to their adequacy score. This can stack to 20% if Telehealth and CON are met. 5. Enter a Geography. Typing the first two letters, gives you a list of counties, states. You can select a maximum of 5 counties or states. If both Adequacy and Accessibility are enabled, see the Adequacy and Accessibility section below for additional details on Geography. 6. Click on the Prepare Analysis button to create the Adequacy Analysis. The created analysis is added to the list on the Manage Adequacy Analyses page. Adequacy and Accessibility When both Adequacy and Accessibility have been enabled, additional options will be available in the New Adequacy Analysis. Adequacy Specification: The Adequacy Specification drop down will have options to create or edit a specification. For details on how to create a new or edit an existing Specification, refer to the Specification help Content. Geography: The geography field allows searches by zip code, accepting both zip5s and zip3s. Note: 5-digit zip codes (e.g., 94114) and 3 digit zip prefixes (e.g., 941*) represent all zip codes starting with 941. Access Methodology: The Access Methodology field appears below the Geography field on the New Adequacy Analysis screen. The Standard option is selected by default. Standard and Compound: • The Standard option measures the time and distance of provider to member, according to the select specification, for each specialty separately. This is what Adequacy will default to and the only method that CMS will accept. For example, do members have access to providers with a specialty of Cardiology? If yes, pass. If no, fail. • The Compound option measures the time and distance of provider to member, according to the select specification, for all specialties together. For example, do members have access to providers with specialties of Cardiology, Endocrinology, and Pediatrics? If yes, pass. If no, fail.
  Analysis Results Page Click on the adequacy analysis file name on the Manage Adequacy Analyses list page to view the analysis results. The Analysis Results page is displayed. The Analysis Results page provides an Overview tab and Map tab. The Show/Hide Analysis Criteria links is a toggle link that displays all the criteria entered/selected for the analysis. The top portion of the Analysis Results provides the number of Passes and Fails by Counties. Green indicates standards set in the Specification for Adequacy analysis have passed, Yellow indicates standards set in the Specification for Adequacy analysis failed but can be resolved , and Red indicates standards set in the Specification for Adequacy analysis failed and cannot be resolved. See Summary by Geography below for more information on resolving gaps in Adequacy analysis. Overview Tab The Overview tab displays a summary of the Adequacy analysis which includes the Provider and Access Requirements, and the number passed or failed for each network and for each county present in the selected Geography. When you click on any network name, detailed analysis of the status of the Provider and Access Requirements and their Overall Adequacy status in Summary by Geography page. See Summary by Geography below for more information. Map Tab The Map tab displays the analysis results on a map using shaded areas to indicate the Adequacy status. When you hover over a highlighted area, you can see the status (meets or fails adequacy) of the Provider and Access requirements. When you click on a highlighted area, you can see the detailed analysis of the status of the Provider and Access Requirements and their Overall Adequacy status in Summary by Geography page for that Geography. See Summary by Geography below for more information. Summary by Geography Page You can navigate to the Summary by Geography page from both the Overview and Map tabs by selecting a network in the selected county. You can see the detailed analysis of the Provider and Access Requirements and their Overall Adequacy status stating whether adequacy was met by the specialty for that network in the county or state selected. This analysis is derived from using the standards from the specification file used during the Adequacy creation. The columns, CON (Certificate of Need) and Telehealth are bonuses . If there is a provider with that specialty, the bonus will display in that column. You can select the status and specialty for refined results. By Status: In the Summary by Geography view, the Met column provides access to a Recruitment report when you click the battery icon next to a No result. Recruitment report is displayed in Recruitment > Summary Results page. This helps in identifying providers for filling the gap shown as per the Adequacy specifications. For more details on recruiting the providers, refer to Recruitment help content. Note: Providers identified through recruitment that may help close a gap can be added to your Model Network outside of the Adequacy Module. Providers shown in the recruitment summary are potential candidates only and are not confirmed to fill the gap. By Specialty: Exporting Analysis When you click on the Export button, a PDF of the analysis will be downloaded. When you click on the dropdown in the Export button, you can also download the CSV files with required details like County Details, Specialty Details, Provider HSD Template and Facility HSD Template. The Provider HSD Template and Facility HSD Template are the CSV templates that can be exported and submitted to CMS, where HSD stands for Health Service Delivery. For more details on HSD, refer to HSD from Glossary. Certain columns in these CSV export file will be blank and must be completed manually before submitting for CMS Compliance verification. Here is an example for the downloaded Provider HSD .csv file. The columns in which data does not populate automatically in Provider HSD are: 1. If PCP, Accepts New Patients? (Y/N) 2. RPPO-Specific Exception to Written Agreements? (Y/N) 3. Letter of Intent? (Y/N) Only applicable for MA Applicants Here is an example for the downloaded Facility HSD .csv file. The columns in which data does not populate automatically in Facility HSD are: 1. RPPO-Specific Exception to Written Agreements? (Y/N) 2. Letter of Intent? (Y/N) Only applicable for MA Applicants
